title: Trace compactification for client-side latency analysis
content:
Context and motivation:

- Problem: customers frequently report perceived slowness that doesn’t show up in our server-side 95/99 p99 metrics. Root cause is often split between client serialization, network, and tiny server microspans that get lost when we store full spans at 1x size for every request (trace volume -> cost).
- Goal: design a low-cost, high-signal tracing strategy that preserves enough client-side detail for debugging perceived latency while controlling storage/query cost and respecting sampling budgets.

High-level approach: compactify at ingestion, add client-side delta markers, and tier storage.

1) Compact trace model (proposal)
- Record three tiers of information from the client + server:
  * session anchors (session_id, user_tier, tenant_id) – always kept
  * compact timeline events – delta-encoded timestamps: client_send, client_recv, http_request_start, http_request_end, kv_cache_lookup, kv_cache_hit, model_forward_start, model_forward_end, token_emit_start, token_emit_end
  * optional verbose spans – full spans for server-side critical path only (e.g., > 200ms or flagged by probe)
- Compression rules: store deltas in ms, use enum codes for common events, coalesce repeated events (e.g., repeated small token emits) into aggregated counters plus first/last timestamps.
- Benefit: reduces trace payload by ~6-10x in prototype while keeping causal ordering and per-component latencies.

2) Instrumentation and span tagging (what to add in code)
- Client SDK (browser & mobile): add session_anchor, client_wall_time, client_request_id (uuid), sdk_version, region, experiment_flag
- Edge/proxy: annotate request with upstream_client_request_id and earliest observed client_time to compute network delta
- Server runtime: add structured fields to spans: model_variant, kv_cache_hit (true/false), batch_size, request_priority, pinned_model_version
- Standard tags enum (short keys): "s"=session, "c"=client_ts_delta_ms, "k"=kv_hit, "b"=batch, "m"=model_ms

3) Sampling + retention policy
- Default adaptive sampling: 1% of all traces stored as full verbose traces per tenant; additional 4% stored as compactified traces with timeline events; certain triggers force full capture: p99 latency per-tenant spike, manual operator mark, canary traffic, model fallback events.
- Retention tiers: compact traces retained 7d, full traces retained 30d for critical tenants (SLA customers), aggregated counters indefinitely (90d).

4) Dashboard & query design notes (low-cost investigation surfaces)
- New widgets to add to per-tenant dashboards:
  * Client perceived latency heatmap (bucketed by client->edge network + server processing): show median/90/99 of client_recv - client_send (client wall) minus edge delta
  * Compact-trace timeline explorer: lightweight UI that renders delta-encoded events with zoom; clicking a span shows full verbose trace if present
  * KV cache warmth panel: percent kv_hit per tenant, distribution of kv_hit latency, cold-start rate by model and tenant (30m window)
  * Aggregated token path attribution: stacked bar of time (kv lookup / model forward / token emit / network) per percentile
- Query guidelines: prefer pre-aggregated metrics for dashboard panels; only use trace store for deep-dive. Default dashboards must use 1m-5m rollups with a heavy emphasis on percentiles and tail buckets (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 where feasible).

5) Metrics definitions (explicit)
- client_perceived_latency_ms: (client_recv - client_send) median/p90/p99 (be explicit whether includes network)
- network_rtt_ms: (edge_receive_ts - client_send_ts) median/p90/p99
- server_processing_ms: aggregated server-side spans (model+kv+orchestration) median/p90/p99
- kv_cache_hit_rate: (# kv_cache_hit == true) / (# kv_cache_lookup) computed per-model, per-tenant
- batch_size_avg: average infer batch size per minute, per model pool
- token_throughput_per_gpu: tokens/s across pool, used for cost SLI
- token_emit_latency_ms: time from model_forward_end to first token_emit_end

6) Trace collection playbook (investigation steps)
- Step 0: reproduce with synthetic probe (see probe templates) capturing client-side marker.
- Step 1: check per-tenant client_perceived_latency_ms and network_rtt_ms panels. If network delta is large, escalate to infra networking.
- Step 2: if server_processing_ms high, open compact-trace timeline on representative sample; check for kv cache misses and batch stalls.
- Step 3: if kv_cache_hit_rate low for slow requests, correlate with model version and recent rollouts.
- Step 4: surface full trace for a handful of p99 events (operator can flip capture from compact to full).
- Step 5: if token_emit_latency is abnormal, check kernel selection logs and GPU saturation metrics.

7) Probe design (synthetics to reduce blind spots)
- Probe types: lightweight client-sim probes from multiple regions, heavy path probes that exercise long prompt sequences to stress kv cache and batching, canary probes against new model variants.
- Cadence: global probes every 30s, tenant-specific sampled probes at 5m for high-tier customers, deep-run probes hourly for model pools under active rollout.
- Probe trace payloads should include client markers and request metadata so they become first-class compact traces.

8) Cost & query budgeting rules
- Enforce trace-query quotas per-customer dashboard to avoid runaway ad-hoc trace queries.
- Default dashboards must avoid raw trace JOINs; use precomputed aggregates and materialized views for expensive joins (tenant x model x KV warmth).
- Instrumentation must tag high-cardinality fields (e.g., full prompt text) as ephemeral and not stored in compact traces unless explicitly flagged.

9) Rollout plan and telemetry gating
- Phase 0 (prototype): implement compact schema in ingest pipeline + sample adapters for 2 weeks; run side-by-side with current traces and collect size delta metrics.
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable compactification for 30% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants, add dashboard widgets and operator toggles.
- Phase 2 (opt-in): expose compact trace opt-in for tenants with debug mode; add retention tiers UI in console.

10) Open questions / risks
- Privacy/PII: client-side markers could include user-identifying session anchors; need review by privacy & legal.
- Lossy compression: are we comfortable losing certain microspan boundaries? Define strict criteria for when to keep full spans.
- Cross-region clocks: client timestamps may have skew; need robust delta normalization (edge should attach observed client clock and server clock simultaneously).
- Query UX: operators need fast pivoting between compact and full trace; building this in UI will require caching logic.

Appendix: quick checklist for engineers instrumenting (copy into PR template)
- Add client_request_id to headers and persist across proxies.
- Emit delta markers as short enum-coded events in telemetry envelope.
- Tag spans with kv_cache_hit, batch_size, model_variant, tenant_id (short form).
- Wire server ingestion to run compactification step before storing traces; produce size/ingest delta metric.

Action items (owners):
- Maya Chen: coordinate privacy review and prototype ingest adapter (target end of Q4).
- Arjun Kapoor: implement client SDK delta markers (browser + node).
- Elena Park: dashboard widgets and rollup views (prototype panels).
- Samir Patel: sampling budget enforcement and retention tier config.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please sanity-check the suggested delta-field names (short keys) against existing span schemas to avoid collisions.
- We intentionally prefer coarser signals with predictable storage cost rather than on-demand full capture that explodes trace volume.

References and useful links: see linked_artifacts list at top.
